title: FAFB-FlyWire
text: articles gives quick overview mapping points FAFB14 (used “walled garden” Virtual Fly Brain FlyWire.
code: library(fafbseg) #> Run dr_fafbseg() for a status report on your installation

title: FAFB-FlyWire
text: known points Compare displacements (nm) forward inverse mapping sample neuron. First map points stats quick histogram
code: # identified location in FAFB14 p.fafb.nm <- cbind(477042, 284535, 90680) p.fafb.raw <- p.fafb.nm/c(4,4,40) # corresponding location in FlyWire p.flywire.raw <- cbind(118865, 71338, 2267) p.flywire.nm <- p.flywire.raw * c(4,4,40) # check displacement flywire2fafb(p.flywire.nm)-p.fafb.nm #>      X  Y Z #> [1,] 3 -1 0  # check what happens when you apply the inverse fafb2flywire(p.fafb.nm)-p.flywire.nm #>       X Y Z #> [1,] -3 2 0 data("AV4b1", package='catmaid') before=xyzmatrix(AV4b1) after=fafb2flywire(before) d=sqrt(rowSums((before-after)^2)) summary(d) #>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max.  #>     2.0   287.9   416.0   446.9   559.1  2113.7 hist(d, br=20, main='Displacement /µm') sample_points_in_surf <- function(x, n){   x=as.mesh3d(x)   bb=boundingbox(x)   mm=mapply(runif, min=bb[1,], max=bb[2,], n = n)   colnames(mm)=c("X","Y","Z")   data.frame(mm, inside=pointsinside(mm,x)) } set.seed(42) sxyz=sample_points_in_surf(FAFB14.surf,25000) sxyz.in=subset(sxyz, inside) sxyz.fw=fafb2flywire(xyzmatrix(sxyz.in)) deltas=sxyz.fw-sxyz.in delta=rowSums(deltas[,c("X","Y")]) jet.colors<-colorRampPalette(c('navy','cyan','yellow','red')) nclear3d(); spheres3d(xyzmatrix(sxyz.in), col=jet.colors(10)[cut(delta, breaks = 10)], rad=2000)

title: FAFB-FlyWire
text: Let’s send points back
code: sxyz.fafb2=flywire2fafb(sxyz.fw) deltas=sxyz.fafb2-xyzmatrix(sxyz.in) delta=rowSums(deltas[,c("X","Y")]) hist(delta, main = "Round Trip Error", xlab='delta /nm')

title: FAFB-FlyWire
text: map complex objects, use xform_brain()  Note relevant links: Load flywire mesh plot CATMAID skeleton ’s obvious partially traced, still neuron.
code: AV4b1.fw=xform_brain(AV4b1, sample='FAFB14', reference = 'FlyWire') # find the main branch point of a neuron, a good place to point to mainbranch <- function(x, ...) {   if(is.neuronlist(x))      return(nlapply(x, mainbranch, ...))      sx=nat::simplify_neuron(x, ...)   xyzmatrix(sx)[sx$BranchPoints,] } choose_segmentation("flywire") open_fafb_ngl(mainbranch(AV4b1.fw), coords.only = TRUE) #> [1] "88371.25,40478.75,3668" av4.fwm=read_cloudvolume_meshes('720575940618054533') nclear3d() plot3d(AV4b1.fw, col='red', lwd=3) wire3d(av4.fwm[[1]], col='grey', alpha=.2)

title: Accessing the chunked graph server
text: One goals fafbseg package provide access different 3D segmentations FAFB dataset. Currently available segmentations include FlyWire (based 3D CNNs : U-Net) GoogleBrain (based recursive CNNs : flood-filling networks). Furthermore enable location transfer comparison CATMAID (skeleton based) manual reconstruction. order achieve one needs access 3D segmentations stored graph database Graphene/PyChunkedGraph. also provide Python tool called CloudVolume provides programmatic access graph database.

title: Accessing the chunked graph server
text: manual steps flywire_set_token() tries automate follows Visit https://globalv1.flywire-daf.com/auth/api/v1/refresh_token, Copy token present , let’s say "xxyyzz" create file named cave-secret.json location ~/.cloudvolume/secrets/cave-secret.json. example, Terminal: Paste following contents Save file Now access chunked graph server
code: mkdir -p .cloudvolume/secrets/ touch ~/.cloudvolume/secrets/cave-secret.json open ~/.cloudvolume/secrets/cave-secret.json -e {   "token": "xxyyzz" }

text: make sure one neuron displayed want parse object identifier relationships. text: can use package generate URLs pointing defined location neuroglancer dataset. includes arbitrary locations FAFB dataset specified interactively using CATMAID URLs. example, find location referenced tweet: Zoom @dddavi whole fly brain EM dataset using public @catmaid server hosted @virtualflybrain. whole brain view synaptic detail. Click explore location within mushroom body parallel fibre system ! https://t.co/JxsBGe3RbJ @flyconnectome pic.twitter.com/NfDiXgJOPX can use approach https://flywire.ai URLs additional option transforming coordinates get closer correct location FlyWire assembly FAFB data (typically hundred nm ). code: library(fafbseg) # First, optionally set a package option with an example neuroglancer URL for your dataset. # This URL will define the image layers that are visible. You need to use an # URL for which you have access. The package ships with a default using segmentation # fafb_v14:fafb_v14_16nm_v00c_split3xfill2 which is probably what you need. options(fafbseg.sampleurl="https://<neuroglancerlurl>")  # Now open location specified by CATMAID URL u='https://fafb.catmaid.virtualflybrain.org/?pid=2&zp=131280&yp=170014.98879622458&xp=426584.81386896875&tool=navigator&sid0=2&s0=-1' open_fafb_ngl(u)  # or display raw coordinates that you can paste into active Neuroglancer session open_fafb_ngl(u, coords.only = TRUE) # opens a new browser tab with_segmentation('flywire31',    open_fafb_ngl(u, sample = 'FAFB14', reference = "FlyWire"))  # writes coordinates to clipboard so that you can paste them into an existings # flywire neuroglancer browser tab with_segmentation('flywire31',    clipr::write_clip(     open_fafb_ngl(u, coords.only = TRUE,        sample = 'FAFB14', reference = "FlyWire")))

text: may also want install skeletor, package Philipp Schlegel helps thin skeletonise meshes . can produce accurate results get using TEASAR meshparty, depend either. install, : test skeletor works flywire neurons python using: installed skeletor specified python environment described , R able :
code: $ source activate flywire_env $ conda install nomkl $ pip3 install git+git://github.com/schlegelp/skeletor@master $ pip3 install fastremap $ pip3 install ncollpyde python from cloudvolume import CloudVolume import trimesh as tm import skeletor as sk id=720575940614134045 id=720575940634367221 vol = CloudVolume('graphene://https://prodv1.flywire-daf.com/segmentation/1.0/fly_v31', use_https=True) m = vol.mesh.get(id, deduplicate_chunk_boundaries=False)[id] m = tm.Trimesh(m.vertices, m.faces) simp = sk.pre.simplify(m, ratio=.1) cntr = sk.pre.contract(simp, SL=10, WH0=2, iter_lim=4, epsilon=0.05, precision=1e-6, progress=False, operator='umbrella') swc = sk.skeletonize.by_vertex_clusters(cntr, sampling_dist=500, progress=False) swc = sk.post.clean_up(s = swc, mesh = simp, theta = 0.01) sk.post.radii(s = swc, mesh = simp, method='knn', n=5, aggregate='mean') print(swc)  # Faster, wavefront skeletonisation m = sk.pre.fix_mesh(m, remove_disconnected=10) swc2 = sk.skeletonize.by_wavefront(m, waves=2s) print(swc2) # Skeletonise choose_segmentation("flywire") nx=xform_brain(elmr::dense_core_neurons, ref="FlyWire", sample="FAFB14") xyz =xyzmatrix(nx) ids = unique(flywire_xyz2id(xyz[sample(1:nrow(xyz),100),])) neurons = skeletor(ids)  # Plot in 3D nopen3d() plot3d(neurons) # note, in flywire space, slightly different to FAFBv14 space plot3d(nx, col="black", lwd  =2) # note, in flywire space

title: Mesh to mesh distances
text: range ways done, essentially number local minima distance field find. might also case one “patch” one neuron actually matches several patches neuron. However ’ll just try pick simpler approach example. Let’s take points threshold distance query neuron find geodesic distance (.e. distance along mesh surface) . need bit prep work , make graph representation mesh. Convert LHLN mesh representation Now can find geodesic distance selected nodes. Let’s try clustering distance matrix
code: #' Make an igraph representation of the edge network of a mesh object #' #' @param x A \code{mesh3d} object or an object for which an \code{as.mesh3d} #'   method is defined. As a convenience the first mesh object is extracted when #'   \code{x} is a \code{shapelist3d} object. #' @param ... additional arguments passed to \code{as.mesh3d} #' #' @return a \code{igraph} object whose vertices correspond to the vertices of the #'   original mesh object and whose edges have weights matching the edge lengths #'   in the mesh. #' @export mesh2graph <- function(x, ...) {   if(inherits(x, 'shapelist3d')) x=x[[1]]   if(inherits(x, 'neuronlist')) x=x[[1]]   if(!inherits(x, 'mesh3d')) x=as.mesh3d(x, ...)   if(nrow(x$it)!=3) stop("I only work for triangulat meshes right now")      # make the edge list   v1=x$it[1,]   v2=x$it[2,]   v3=x$it[3,]   el=rbind(cbind(v1,v2), cbind(v1,v3), cbind(v2,v3))   g=igraph::graph_from_edgelist(el, directed = FALSE)      # calculate lengths of each edge   xyz=xyzmatrix(x)   edgelengths = function(v1, v2) {     deltas=xyz[v1,,drop=F]-xyz[v2,,drop=F]     sqrt(rowSums(deltas^2))   }   weights=c(edgelengths(v1,v2), edgelengths(v1,v3), edgelengths(v2,v3))   igraph::E(g)$weight=weights   g } g=mesh2graph(pv4b4) dmat=igraph::distances(g, v=which(kd$nn.dists<100), to = which(kd$nn.dists<100)) dd=hclust(as.dist(dmat)) plot(dd, labels = F) # cut using a height relating to a separation of 3000nm groups=cutree(dd, h=3000) # sample randomises colours so that neighbouring clusters have different colours set.seed(42) groupcols=sample(rainbow(max(groups)))[groups]  nclear3d() spheres3d(xyzmatrix(pv4b4)[kd$nn.dists<100,], col=groupcols, rad=200) wire3d(pv4b4[[1]], col=ifelse(kd$nn.dists<100, 'red', 'black'), type='wire')

title: Convert 3D x,y,z locations in brainmaps volumes to segmentation ids — brainmaps_xyz2id
text: underlying brainmaps API expects raw coordinates .e.   voxel indices. slightly complicated fact different   segmentation, skeleton etc volumes may different associated voxel   dimensions. brainmaps_xyz2id automatically looks voxel   dimension. However may want pass raw coordinates   neuroglancer. generally associated resolution   image data e.g. skeletons may larger (coarser) voxel   size. convenience situation can set rawcoords=TRUE. problems requests failing sporadically, may helpful   know Google keep underlying data live may   spin-time. arbitrary timeout Google end (currently ~ 5s) batching nearby points helps Using chunksize argument retry argument passed   brainmaps_fetch can overcome issues. See   examples.

title: Convert 3D x,y,z locations in brainmaps volumes to segmentation ids — brainmaps_xyz2id
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # Physical location in nm brainmaps_xyz2id(c(433368, 168208, 128480)) # Same location as displayed in neuroglancer brainmaps_xyz2id(c(54171, 21026, 3212), rawcoords=TRUE)  # Raw coodinates for the brainmaps volume in question - don't touch brainmaps_xyz2id(c(433368, 168208, 128480)/c(32,32,40), rawvoxdims=NULL)  library(elmr) # get a manually traced neuron (just keep first and only entry in neuronlist) dl4=read.neurons.catmaid('glomerulus DL4 right')[[1]] # map every node location to segmentation ids dl4.segs=brainmaps_xyz2id(dl4) # remove unmapped locations which get id 0 dl4.segs=setdiff(dl4.segs, 0) # read in corresponding skeletons dl4.skels=read_segments2(dl4.segs) # read in corresponding skeletons after including agglomeration merge groups dl4.allskels=read_segments2(find_merged_segments(dl4.segs))  ## retries / cache / chunksize issues # set small chunk size dl4.segs=brainmaps_xyz2id(dl4, chunksize=500) # use retries in case of failure dl4.segs=brainmaps_xyz2id(dl4, chunksize=500, retry=3) # cache successful requests (if you might need to repeat) dl4.segs=brainmaps_xyz2id(dl4, chunksize=500, retry=3, cache=TRUE) } # }

TRUE (default), collapses multi-select columns comma-separated strings. Passed flytable_query. base Optional base name table name ambiguous (exists multiple bases). limit optional limit total number rows returned, applies specify limit directly sql query. default seatable limits SQL queries 100 rows. increase limit 100000 rows default. See paginate interacts server's per-call row cap.

title: Find FlyWire root or supervoxel (leaf) ids for XYZ locations — flywire_xyz2id
text: root ids define whole neuron segmented object. supervoxel ids   correspond small group voxels assumed must belong   object. supervoxel ids change given segmentation,   whereas root ids change every time neuron edited. stable way   refer FlyWire neuron choose nice safe location   arbour (recommend major branch point) store location   supervoxel id. can rapidly map supervoxel id current root id   using flywire_rootid. November 2020, default approach look supervoxel ids   3D point using   spine   transform-service API. order 100x faster mapping via   cloudvolume (since must make single web request every point)   Eric Perlman optimised layout underlying data rapid   mapping. Note using slower cloudvolume method (may still required   volumes fast lookup via spine available)   finding supervoxel given XYZ location order 3x faster   finding root id agglomeration super voxels   given object. Perhaps less intuitively, want look many root   ids, actually quicker flywire_xyz2id(,root=F) followed   flywire_rootid since function can look many root   ids single call ChunkedGraph server. happens   setting fast_root=TRUE, default.

code: fw_url=with_segmentation('flywire31', getOption('fafbseg.sampleurl')) ngl_add_colours(fw_url, colours=c("720575940614404544"="red")) #> neuroglancer scene with 2 layers and 2 segments (of which 2 shown) #>                                 name                    type archived visible #> 1                   Production-image                   image    FALSE    TRUE #> 2 Production-segmentation_with_graph segmentation_with_graph    FALSE    TRUE #>   nsegs nhidden #> 1     0       0 #> 2     2       0 #>                                                                        source #> 1 precomputed://gs://microns-seunglab/drosophila_v0/alignment/image_rechunked #> 2          graphene://https://prod.flywire-daf.com/segmentation/table/fly_v31  if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # colour all neurons in the URL on the clipboard red. # Then convert back to URL and open in default browser browseURL(as.character(ngl_add_colours(clipr::read_clip(), col="red")))  # Let's colour neurons from these 3 scenes in red, green and blue u1="https://ngl.flywire.ai/?json_url=https://globalv1.flywire-daf.com/nglstate/5695474417795072" u2="https://ngl.flywire.ai/?json_url=https://globalv1.flywire-daf.com/nglstate/5198787572137984" u3="https://ngl.flywire.ai/?json_url=https://globalv1.flywire-daf.com/nglstate/5673953041317888" # sequentially build up a data.frame with the colour information # note that col will be recycled to the same length as the number of segments colourdf=data.frame(ids=ngl_segments(u1), col='red') colourdf=rbind(colourdf, data.frame(ids=ngl_segments(u2), col='green')) colourdf=rbind(colourdf, data.frame(ids=ngl_segments(u3), col='blue')) # apply that to the first URL sc=ngl_add_colours(u1, colourdf) browseURL(as.character(sc)) } # }

text: pipeline: 1. Reads specified meshes CloudVolume source. 2. Simplifies mesh (python: skeletor.pre.simplify) 3. Contract mesh (python: skeletor.pre.contract) 4. Skeletonises mesh (python: skeletor.skeletonize) 5. Optionally, cleans mesh (python: skeletor.post.clean_up) 6. Optionally, add radius information skeleton (python:   skeletor.post.radii) 7. Optionally, heal skeleton breaks   (nat::stitch_neurons_mst) 8. Optionally, attempts re-root neuron 'hairball', .e.   approximate soma (reroot_hairball). therefore need working python3 install skeletor,   uses CloudVolume. require meshparty. Please install   Python skeletor module described :   https://github.com/schlegelp/skeletor. must ensure   using python3 (implicitly explicitly) mesh fetching graphene   servers depends . normally work: pip3 install   git+git://github.com/schlegelp/skeletor@master. already   installed skeletor found, recommend editing   Renviron file set environment variable pointing   correct Python. can usethis::edit_r_environ()   setting e.g. RETICULATE_PYTHON="/usr/local/bin/python3".   (Though best practice create conda environment   natverse R sessions direct R using environ file.) need set kind authentication order fetch   volume data skeletonisation. See   https://github.com/seung-lab/cloud-volume#chunkedgraph-secretjson   get token save . can either save json snippet   ~/.cloudvolume/secrets/cave-secret.json set   environment variable (CHUNKEDGRAPH_SECRET="XXXX". Finally also need set option pointing server.   server hosting mesh data interested . might look   something like:   options(fafbseg.cloudvolume.url='graphene://https://xxx.dynamicannotationframework.com/segmentation/xxx/xxx')    can easily add startup Rprofile   usethis::edit_r_profile(). example, flywire data set,   currently:   'graphene://https://prodv1.flywire-daf.com/segmentation/1.0/fly_v31'. Roughly decreasing order impact speed: Ratio: lower ratio = less vertices = faster epsilon: lower target contraction rate = less steps = faster SL: faster contraction = pot. less steps target contraction rate =   faster precision: lower precision = faster least-square computation = faster sampling_dist: larger dist = faster collapse mesh skeleton = faster

title: fafbseg 0.15.17
text: Changes: flytable_cached_table() now defaults expiry = 0 (300), always checking updates see latest metadata default. check still cheap delta-syncs rows changed since last fetch. Pass positive expiry trust cache within window. cam_meta() gains explicit expiry refresh arguments (defaulting expiry = 0, refresh = FALSE) rather passing .... (#252)

title: fafbseg 0.15.16
text: Performance: pandas2df() converts pandas frames large nullable Int64/UInt64 id columns ~20x faster. reticulate::py_to_r() walks extension columns cell cell (~60s 330k-row synapse frame); columns now stringified via fast bit64 path first filtered py_to_r() pass, cutting conversion frame ~60s ~2.5s. Output byte--byte identical. Speeds flywire_partner_summary() / cf_partners() CAVE query returning many rows (#251).

title: fafbseg 0.15.15
text: New features: flywire_key_point() picks good “key” point (major branch point L2 skeleton) associate annotations, key_point_from_neuron() exposes underlying pure neuron helper. Moved aedes package can shared across flywire-style datasets (aedes, crantr).

title: fafbseg 0.15.14
text: Bug fixes: pandas2df() longer loses 64-bit ids nullable Int64/UInt64 column contains missing value. pandas_series_character_values() read cells Series.map(str), upcasts column float64 stringifying, ids came back scientific notation integer64 rescue collapsed whole column NA. now uses Series.astype("str"), stringifies integer cells exactly. Pre-existing independent caveclient convert-flag fix 0.15.13.

title: fafbseg 0.15.13
text: Bug fixes: CAVE queries longer lose 64-bit ids caveclient 8.x / pandas 2.2.x. pandas_series_character_values() converted unconditionally py_to_r(), errors series carrying reticulate’s convert flag $tolist() already returned R vector. error swallowed, bit64::integer64 rescue pandas2df_inmem() silently skipped, nullable Int64 id columns arrived R integer every value overflowed NA (#246). flywire_partner_summary(method = "cave") longer reports unrelated warnings "Synapse query exceeded row limit!" discards result. genuine row-limit warning now; anything else passed query kept (#246).

title: fafbseg 0.15.12
text: New features enhancements: flywire_ids() gains na.rm argument (default FALSE) drops missing (NA) input ids coercion, longer surface null segment "0". Genuine "0"/zero inputs kept. Useful callers crantr::crant_ids() read root ids tables containing incomplete rows. cam_meta() gains drop_status argument controlling status tokens dropped query/join/unique step (default c("duplicate", "bad_nucleus"), ). Matching now case-insensitive token-wise, also handles multi-select status columns holding comma-separated tokens — e.g. downstream callers crantr::crant_meta() can pass drop_status = "DUPLICATED" filter CRANT’s capitalised multi-select duplicate marker.

title: fafbseg 0.15.11
text: New features enhancements: flytable_query() gains chunksize argument force LIMIT/OFFSET pagination fixed-size windows (advanced use; default NULL continues auto-detect server’s per-call cap). flytable_full_fetch() gains control internal page loop. Bug fixes: Fix silent row truncation flytable tables larger server’s SQL query row cap. Seatable’s SQL endpoint silently caps single call server-specific maximum (documented default 10,000 rows SELECT queries, https://api.seatable.com/reference/limits; self-hosted servers may allow ) error truncation signal. flytable_query() now paginates transparently LIMIT/OFFSET default (new paginate argument) returns full result rather truncated one; small results queries pin limit/offset still cost single request. hit practice cloud.seatable.io-hosted CRANTb_meta table (12,652 rows), though self-hosted Cambridge flytable server (raises caps 100,000). API discover given server’s configured cap, pagination self-adapts whatever turns . flytable_full_fetch() (used flytable_cached_table() therefore cam_meta()) now pages table known row count, cold fetch table larger server’s per-call cap longer silently truncated. Fix related pagination bug flytable_list_rows(): page-fetch loop stopped soon page came back fewer rows requested, assumption meant end table. fact list-rows endpoint also enforces per-call page-size cap (documented default 1000 rows, also server-configurable) regardless requested, short page mean table exhausted. loop now continues receives genuinely empty page. Full Changelog: https://github.com/natverse/fafbseg/compare/v0.15.10…v0.15.11

title: fafbseg 0.15.10
text: New features enhancements: cam_meta() gains translate_ids argument brings explicitly supplied root ids forward requested version/timestamp matching, stale ids longer silently drop result. ids fail match mapped table translated (ids already current cost nothing); forced TRUE version/timestamp, ids aligned table’s sync time (mtime) rather live ‘now’. default (NA) enables whenever version/timestamp supplied. (#243) flytable_update_rows() / flytable_append_rows() gain multi-select column write support, splitting comma-separated strings list cells multi-select columns expect. (#242) flywire_nuclei() updated query semantics, now preferring materialized nucleus tables supporting Aedes. (#238) flywire_partner_summary() (CAVE backend) can restrict partners surface via surf / invert_surf. (6f5c659) Quieter behaviour: cam_meta() longer emits “bad supervoxel” warnings supplied ids simply present table; missing ids handled quietly. (#239) Python caveclient logging quietened. Bug fixes: chunk vcache_mset() avoid bit64 .list protection-stack overflow large writes. (#240) flywire_attributes() now reliably returns numeric values (fixes l2cache_normalise_table() bug affecting L2 attribute types). fix dbplyr temp-table name collision surfaced examples. (#237) Full Changelog: https://github.com/natverse/fafbseg/compare/v0.15.9…v0.15.10

title: fafbseg 0.15.9
text: fix pandas2df() -memory conversion object-dtype columns. reticulate’s py_to_r() returns object columns R list length-1 vectors even every cell scalar Python type, per-cell PyLong → int32_t truncation silently corrupts integer values >= 2^31. Surfaces clearly flywire_l2attributes() results, caveclient.l2cache.get_l2data_table() packs scalar attributes (notably size_nm3 area_nm2) Python ints object columns – soma-bearing L2 chunks routinely exceed uint32-max came wrong (<list><int [1]>> shapes). Object columns whose cells scalar Python type now flattened atomic vectors via series.map(str) round-trip (numeric, bit64::integer64 beyond 2^53), preserving arbitrary precision. (#236) Full Changelog: https://github.com/natverse/fafbseg/compare/v0.15.8…v0.15.9

title: fafbseg 0.15.8
text: add FlyWire level-2 cache helpers: flywire_l2attributes(), flywire_l2cache_metadata(), flywire_has_l2cache(), flywire_l2volume(). provide direct access caveclient.l2cache, including datastack-aware lookup L2 ids, optional expansion multi-valued attributes columns, cached root-level volume summaries based size_nm3. flywire_l2ids() now accepts explicit datastack_name, passed new L2 cache wrappers non-default segmentations handled consistently. improve pandas--R conversion used reticulate-backed workflows: pandas2df() gains keep_index=TRUE callers need pandas index preserved first column, -memory conversion path now robust 64-bit integer datetime columns. harden Python environment setup CI ensuring reticulate conda environment pip available reusing selected Python interpreter across later check, coverage, pkgdown steps. additional CI/test robustness current macOS FlyWire-dependent checks, including longer R CMD check timeout graceful skips live FlyWire services unavailable. Full Changelog: https://github.com/natverse/fafbseg/compare/v0.15.7…v0.15.8

title: fafbseg 0.15.7
text: flytable_login(), flytable_base(), flytable_set_token() now read default url getOption("fafbseg.flytable.url", ...), allowing alternative seatable instances (e.g. cloud.seatable.io) used without per-call argument propagation. Downstream packages (e.g. crantr) can wire cam_meta() seatables via with_xxx() wrapper sets option temporarily overrides FLYTABLE_TOKEN (example withr::with_envvar()). flytable_base_impl() now propagates url argument flytable_login() login resulting memoised base agree. cam_meta() gains token argument. supplied, FLYTABLE_TOKEN environment variable swapped via withr::local_envvar() duration call can authenticate alternative seatable instance without permanently overwriting default flytable token. fix overflow check pyids2bit64() bit64 >= 4.8.0, longer auto-coerces character RHS == now returns NA (warning) --range character input rather silently clamping maxint64. previously caused cascading failures across flywire_rootid(), flywire_xyz2id() etc. non-numeric argument binary operator. new internal int64_overflows() helper papers version difference, id2char() now emits warning input overflow int64. #229 fix ngl_encode_url() (therefore flywire_expandurl() / ngl_decode_scene() short URLs) body long raw JSON string. tools::file_ext() calling basename() body, errors path long recent R; now treat body file path plausibly one. #229 Full Changelog: https://github.com/natverse/fafbseg/compare/v0.15.6…v0.15.7
